lessons.title: Lines can be many kinds
objectives: Make marks with straight, curly, wavy and zigzag lines
Use lines to fill a leaf shape

keywords.def: a mark made by moving a pencil along the paper
a line that goes sharply up and down
a line that curves up and down like waves
how something feels, such as rough or smooth

starter: Bismillah. Draw a circle in the air with your finger.
What shapes can you see on your screen?
Name one colour you used last year.

teach.heading: Bismillah and our lines
bullets: Every drawing starts with a line
A line can be straight or curved
Take care with your pencil and paper
teach.note: Pupils need a pencil, a crayon and paper. Say bismillah. Show a straight line and a curly line on screen.

teach.heading: Types of line
teach.note: Draw each on a board and name it. Children copy in the air first, then on paper. Misconception: a line must be straight.

teach.heading: Lines in nature
bullets: A leaf has veins that look like lines
teach.note: Show a real leaf if possible. Ask what lines they see. Link to Allah's creation: attention to detail.

teach.heading: Fill the shape
bullets: Use a different line in each part
teach.note: Model drawing a leaf outline then adding three kinds of line. Encourage patience; no rubbing out needed.

practice: Draw a wavy line, then a zigzag line.
Find one straight line in your room.
independent: Draw a leaf and fill it with at least three different lines.
Fill a page with a spiral of thick and thin lines.
exit: Which line goes up and down sharply?
lessons.homework: Look at a plant or tree at home and draw the lines you see.
lessons.send: SEND: trace over dotted lines first; EAL: pair each line with its word and a gesture; stretch: add pattern inside every part of the leaf.

lessons.title: Rubbings and textures
objectives: Put textures together in a collage drawing

keywords.def: how a surface feels, such as rough or smooth
a picture made by rubbing crayon over paper on top of an object
bumpy, not smooth
flat and even to touch

starter: Name two kinds of line from last lesson.
Is a cushion rough or smooth?
Say bismillah and stroke your hand along your desk. What does it feel like?

teach.heading: Touch and describe
teach.note: Ask children to find a safe object (cloth, leaf, coin). Check no sharp or dirty items. Take turns describing.

teach.heading: Making a rubbing
bullets: Put paper on top of the object
Rub with the side of a crayon
The pattern appears on the page
teach.note: Model with a coin or leaf under thin paper. Hold the paper still with the other hand. Use the side of the crayon, not the tip.

teach.heading: Many textures, one picture
bullets: Make three rubbings on one page
Cut or fold to make a collage
teach.note: If no scissors, tear the paper carefully. Remind about safety; adult to help with scissors.

teach.heading: Show what we made
teach.note: Choose 4 children to describe their favourite texture.

practice: Is a stone rough or smooth?
Draw a wavy line and a zigzag line.
independent: Make rubbings of three different surfaces and label each.
Make a rubbing leaf picture and colour around it.
exit: Name one rough thing and one smooth thing.
How do you make a rubbing?
lessons.homework: Make a rubbing of something outside your home, with a grown-up.
lessons.send: SEND: grown-up holds the paper; EAL: label textures with a picture word list; stretch: sort rubbings into rough and smooth sets.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Printing and a space buggy (Moon Zoom! and Rain & Sunrays)
lessons.title: Printing rain and sun patterns
lessons.bigQuestion: How can one small tile make a whole pattern?
objectives: To understand how a printing tile makes a repeating pattern
successCriteria: All: make a print with a tile
Most: print a pattern that repeats
Some: change the colour to make a new pattern
lessons.smsc: Cultural: repeating patterns in Islamic art

keywords.def: a picture made by pressing something with paint on it
a flat piece we print with
a small shape used again and again
do the same again
shapes in an order that repeats

hook.text: Look at a tiled floor or a wallpaper. Where does the pattern start again?

islamicLink.text: Allah sends the rain and makes the sun shine. Muslim artists showed the beauty of Allah's creation with patterns that repeat again and again, on tiles and walls. Allah is al-Musawwir, the Fashioner of every shape (al-Hashr 59:24).

starter.q: Is a tile of card hard or soft?
Name one kind of winter weather.
starter.a: For example: rain, frost, wind, snow

teach.heading: What is a print?
bullets: We press the tile on paper
The shape stays on the paper
teach.note: Show a potato or card print. Press, lift, look. Ask: what do you see? The tile's shape.

teach.heading: Rain and sun motifs
bullets: Make the motif from string on card
teach.note: Glue string in a raindrop or sun shape on a square of card. Let it dry. The string makes a raised line that prints.

teach.heading: Make it repeat
teach.note: Islamic art uses repeating patterns on tiles and walls. Show a photo of tiles. Ask: what repeats?

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

check.why: Only the first one repeats the same order again.

practice.q: What comes next? sun, rain, sun, rain, ...
practice.model:
Say it aloud: sun, rain, sun, rain.
The pattern goes back to sun.
Next is sun.

practice.q: What do we do after pressing the tile?
What makes the raised line on our tile?

independent.q: Core: Make a sun or rain tile with string and card. Print it four times in a line.
independent.a: A line of four prints of the same motif
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: thin paint on the tile, press on the paper, lift straight up, move along one gap.

independent.q: Extend: Print a sun, rain, sun, rain pattern.
independent.a: Two tiles printed in an ABAB repeat

independent.q: Stretch: Print a second row in a new colour.
independent.a: Two rows, two colours

exit.q: A motif is:
exit.a: A) a small shape used again and again
options: A small shape used again and again

exit.q: Big question: how can one small tile make a whole pattern?
exit.a: We print it again and again in the same order

lessons.homework: Make a printing tile from card and string and print a repeating pattern on scrap paper.
lessons.send: SEND: a ready-made tile and a sponge dabber; adult holds the paper. EAL: press, lift, repeat with actions. Stretch: make a pattern with three motifs.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 1 curriculum map and long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack, Topic, Spring 1 Moon Zoom! (Cornerstones Maestro: CHECK IN MAESTRO) (art and design strand)
Home practical guide: printing tiles with card, string and paint (portal worksheet); cover the table first
Thick card squares (from a cereal box), string, PVA glue, scissors (adult help)
Poster paint or ready-mixed paint, a plate, scrap paper
An apron or old shirt

pictures.alt: Repeating tile pattern on a wall

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Printing and a space buggy (Moon Zoom! and Rain & Sunrays)
lessons.title: Wheels and axles: design a space buggy
lessons.bigQuestion: Why do wheels need an axle to turn?
objectives: To understand how wheels, axles and a chassis help a vehicle move
successCriteria: All: name a wheel, an axle and a chassis
Most: say what each part does
Some: draw a labelled design of a space buggy
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: wonder at what people can invent with the minds Allah gave them

keywords.def: a round part that turns
the rod the wheels turn on
the base of a vehicle
a plan drawing of what we will make
something that carries people or things

hook.text: What would a car on the Moon need that a car at home does not?

islamicLink.text: Allah gave people animals to ride and carry loads, and says He creates things we do not yet know (an-Nahl 16:8). People later used their minds to invent wheels, cars and even a buggy for the Moon.

starter.q: Is a metal rod bendy or stiff?
Who was the first person on the Moon?

teach.heading: Look at a toy car
teach.note: Pupils turn a toy car over on camera. Ask: what holds the wheels on?

teach.heading: Three parts
bullets: Axle: the rod through the wheels
teach.note: Point to each part on a toy. Wheels and axles are a mechanism: they make movement.

teach.heading: A real Moon buggy
bullets: Astronauts drove a buggy on the Moon in 1971
teach.note: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was first used on the Apollo 15 mission in 1971. Show the photo (no people). Ask: what do you notice?

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

options: The rod the wheels turn on
check.why: The base is the chassis. The axle is the rod through the wheels.

practice.q: Label the base of a vehicle.
practice.model:
The flat part at the bottom holds everything.
It is the chassis.

practice.q: What turns on the axle?
How many axles does a car with four wheels usually have?

independent.q: Core: Draw your space buggy design. Label the wheels, axles and chassis.
independent.a: A drawing with three labels in the right places
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: a box for the chassis, two straws for axles, four circles for wheels, then the labels.

independent.q: Extend: Choose a material for each part from a box, straws and bottle tops.
independent.a: Chassis: box; axles: straws or skewers; wheels: bottle tops

independent.q: Stretch: Add one thing your buggy needs for the Moon.
independent.a: For example: a box to carry Moon rocks or an aerial

exit.q: Wheels are:
exit.a: A) round

exit.q: Big question: why do wheels need an axle to turn?
exit.a: The axle holds the wheels on and lets them spin

lessons.homework: Collect a small box, two straws and four bottle tops for next lesson's buggy.
lessons.send: SEND: a real toy car to hold and label stickers. EAL: wheel, axle, chassis with pictures. Stretch: explain why the wheels must be the same size.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 1 curriculum map and long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack, Topic, Spring 1 Moon Zoom! (Cornerstones Maestro: CHECK IN MAESTRO) (DT strand)
Space buggy design sheet with label boxes (portal printable)
A toy car to look at
Pencil and coloured pencils

pictures.alt: A replica of the Moon buggy
The wheels and axles under a toy car
The rocky surface of the Moon

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Printing and a space buggy (Moon Zoom! and Rain & Sunrays)
lessons.title: Make and test a space buggy
lessons.bigQuestion: How can we make our buggy roll further?
objectives: To understand how to make, test and improve a simple vehicle
successCriteria: All: make a buggy that rolls
Most: test how far it rolls
Some: say one way to make it better
lessons.smsc: Moral: honest testing and trying again

keywords.def: build what we designed
try it to see if it works
say what went well and what to change
the rod the wheels turn on
the base of a vehicle

hook.text: Your buggy will not roll. What could be wrong?

islamicLink.text: Allah loves that when one of us does a job, we do it well and carefully. We make our buggy with care, test it honestly and try again. Trying our best is part of good character (ihsan).

starter.q: The base of a buggy is the:

starter.a: Holds the wheels and lets them turn

starter.q: What did you collect for today?
starter.a: A box, two straws and four bottle tops

teach.heading: Make the axles
bullets: Push two straws through the box
teach.note: Show how an adult makes holes with a pencil in a small box. The straws must be level and parallel.

teach.heading: Add the wheels
bullets: An adult makes a hole in each bottle top
Push a skewer or straw through
teach.note: Safety: adults use sharp things. Wheels must not rub on the box.

teach.heading: Test it
bullets: Let it roll down a book ramp
teach.note: Same ramp and same push each time to keep it fair.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share results.

check.q: The wheels rub on the box. What should we do?
options: Move the wheels a little away from the box
check.why: Wheels need a gap so they can turn freely.

practice.q: Our buggy rolled 3 hand spans, then 5, then 4. Which roll was best?
practice.model:
Look at the numbers: 3, 5, 4.
The biggest is 5.
So the second roll went furthest.

practice.q: Why do we use the same ramp each time?
Who makes the holes?

independent.q: Core: Make your buggy and test it on a book ramp three times.
independent.a: A working buggy and three hand-span results
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: book ramp, put the buggy at the top, let go (no push), count hand spans.

independent.q: Extend: Say one thing that went well.
independent.a: For example: the wheels turned freely

independent.q: Stretch: Say one thing you would change.
independent.a: For example: straighter axles, bigger wheels, a lighter box

exit.q: Evaluate means:
exit.a: A) say what went well and what to change
options: Say what went well and what to change

exit.q: Big question: how can we make our buggy roll further?
exit.a: For example: make the axles straight and let the wheels turn freely

lessons.homework: Test your buggy on a different floor (carpet, then a smooth floor) and tell an adult where it rolled further.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-made holes and wheels; pupil assembles and tests. EAL: make, test, change with actions. Stretch: test a bigger and smaller wheel and compare.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 1 curriculum map and long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack, Topic, Spring 1 Moon Zoom! (Cornerstones Maestro: CHECK IN MAESTRO) (DT strand)
Home practical guide and safety card: the space buggy (portal worksheet); an adult makes every hole
A small box, two straws, two wooden skewers (adult only), four bottle tops, sticky tape
A book to make a ramp
Buggy test record: three hand-span results (portal printable)

pictures.alt: A small cardboard box for the chassis

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Observational drawing and a memory box (Memory Box)
lessons.title: Drawing a treasured object
lessons.bigQuestion: How can a pencil make something look shiny or soft?
objectives: To understand how to draw what we see using light and dark shading
successCriteria: All: draw the outline of the object
Most: shade light and dark parts
Some: use hard and soft pencils for different tones
lessons.crossCurricular: History: objects as clues about the past
lessons.smsc: Cultural: objects that hold family memories

keywords.def: look very carefully
the line round the edge of a shape
colour in with a pencil to show dark parts
how light or dark something is
very special to us

hook.text: Which object in your home is special to your family? Why?

starter.q: An artefact is an object from the:

starter.a: For example: wood, metal, glass, plastic

teach.heading: Look first
teach.note: Use a cup or an old watch. Ask: what shape is it? Where is it dark?

teach.heading: Light and dark
teach.note: Show a tone strip: five boxes from light to dark.

teach.heading: Draw with me
teach.note: Model drawing a mug on camera.

model.answer: A mug with light and dark tones

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.q: To make a dark tone, press:
check.why: Pressing harder puts more pencil on the paper, so it looks darker.

practice.q: Make a tone strip: five boxes, light to dark.
practice.model:
Box 1: press very softly.
Box 2: a little harder.
Keep pressing harder.
Box 5: press hard. Darkest.

practice.q: Where does the light shine on your object?
practice.a: For example: the top of the cup

independent.q: Core: Draw your treasured object. Outline, details, then shading.
independent.a: A drawing with an outline and two or more tones
independent.model: Teacher draws the outline of the mug again slowly and talks through it.

independent.q: Extend: Use a soft pencil (2B) for the darkest parts.
independent.a: Darker tones in the shadow

independent.q: Stretch: Write why the object is special.
independent.a: For example: My grandad's watch reminds us of him

exit.q: 'Observe' means:
exit.a: Look very carefully

exit.q: Big question: how can a pencil make something look shiny?
exit.a: Leave white paper for the shine and shade the dark parts

lessons.homework: Draw one more object from home with three tones of shading.
lessons.send: SEND: thick pencil and a simple object such as a cup. EAL: light, dark, press with actions. Stretch: draw the shadow under the object. No drawing of people or faces.
resources: Tarbiyyah Primary Year 1 curriculum map and long-term plans 2023-24; TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack, Topic, Spring 2 Memory Box (companion: Human Senses) (Cornerstones Maestro: CHECK IN MAESTRO)
Tone strip and drawing frame sheet (portal printable)
HB and 2B pencils if available, rubber
A treasured object from home (a cup, a watch, a box)

pictures.alt: A pencil tone scale from light to dark

lessons.unit: Spring 2: Observational drawing and a memory box (Memory Box)
lessons.title: Make a memory box (DT)
lessons.bigQuestion: What three things would you keep in a box to tell your story?
objectives: To understand how to design, make and improve a box that holds our memories
successCriteria: All: make and decorate a box
Most: join parts firmly
Some: say what you would improve
lessons.crossCurricular: History: objects that tell the story of our lives

keywords.def: plan what we will make
fix parts together
make it look special
say what is good and what to improve
something we remember

hook.text: If you had a memory box, what would you put in it first?

starter.a: What, where, when, who or how

teach.heading: Design
teach.note: Show a design sheet: box shape, pattern, colours.

teach.heading: Make
teach.note: Safety: an adult helps with scissors.

teach.heading: Evaluate
teach.note: Model: 'My box is strong. Even better if the paper was smoother.'

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: We evaluate: say what went well and what to improve.

practice.q: Plan your pattern on the design sheet.
practice.a: A labelled plan with shapes and colours
practice.model:
I draw my box.
I choose stars and moons.
I pick two colours: blue and gold.
I label them.

practice.q: How will you join the paper to the box?

independent.q: Core: Cover and decorate your box. Join parts firmly.
independent.a: A covered, decorated box
independent.model: Teacher covers one side of a box on camera: glue, press, hold for ten seconds.

independent.q: Extend: Add a label with your name and the year.
independent.a: A label on the box

independent.q: Stretch: Say one thing you would improve.
independent.a: For example: smoother paper, a stronger lid

exit.q: Evaluate means:
exit.a: Say what is good and what to improve
options: Say what is good and what to improve

exit.q: Big question: what three things would you keep in your box?
exit.a: Three objects with reasons, for example a first Qur'an, a shell, a drawing

lessons.homework: Finish the memory box and fill it with three objects that tell your story; tell your family why you chose them.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-cut paper shapes; glue stick. EAL: design, make, evaluate with pictures. Stretch: add a hinge with tape for the lid. Adult helps with scissors.

A small cardboard box (shoe box or tea box)
Glue stick, scrap paper, coloured paper, tape
Child-safe scissors with an adult

lessons.unit: Summer 1: City drawing and moving cards (Bright Lights, Big City)
lessons.title: Drawing a London landmark from memory
lessons.bigQuestion: How much can you remember after looking at something for one minute?
objectives: To understand how artists use different lines and detail to draw a building
successCriteria: All: draw with thick, thin, straight and curved lines
Most: draw a landmark from memory
Some: add detail after looking again
lessons.crossCurricular: Geography: London landmarks from our aerial photo lesson
lessons.smsc: Cultural: an artist who notices the beauty of buildings

keywords.def: a mark made by moving a pencil
small parts, like windows
what we keep in our mind
a person who makes art
a building that is easy to spot

hook.text: Could you draw your own front door without looking at it?

starter.a: For example: Tower Bridge, St Paul's Cathedral

teach.heading: Stephen Wiltshire
bullets: He draws whole cities from memory
He looks, then draws every window
teach.note: We look at his city drawings online, not at photos of him. They are buildings and streets.

teach.heading: Kinds of line
teach.note: Draw each line on the board. Pupils copy on their whiteboards.

teach.heading: Look, hide, draw
teach.note: Model with Tower Bridge: towers first, then the road, then windows.

steps: Add windows and points on the towers
model.answer: A line drawing of Tower Bridge

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.q: Small parts like windows are called:
check.why: Detail means the small parts that make a drawing look real.

practice.q: Draw a thick line and a thin line. Show me!
practice.a: A thick line and a thin line
practice.model:
I press hard for a thick line.
I press gently for a thin line.

practice.q: Draw a curved line.
What do we add after looking again?

independent.q: Core: Look at St Paul's Cathedral for one minute, hide it, then draw it from memory using different lines.
independent.a: A memory drawing with a dome and several line types
independent.model: Teacher draws the dome shape first with one curved line.

independent.q: Extend: Look again and add three details.
independent.a: For example: windows, columns, a cross on top

independent.q: Stretch: Name the lines you used.
independent.a: For example: curved for the dome, straight for the columns

exit.q: Stephen Wiltshire draws cities:
exit.a: From memory

exit.q: Big question: how much did you remember after one minute?
exit.a: Pupil says what they remembered and what they added after looking again

lessons.homework: Look at a building near home for one minute, then draw it from memory.
lessons.send: SEND: a dotted outline to trace first. EAL: line words with examples. Stretch: draw the landmark with the River Thames below it.

Photographs of London landmarks (portal slides)
Drawing pencils (soft and hard), paper
Mini-whiteboard and pen

lessons.unit: Summer 1: City drawing and moving cards (Bright Lights, Big City)
lessons.title: A London card that moves
lessons.bigQuestion: How can you make a picture move without batteries?
objectives: To understand how a slider and a lever make parts of a card move
successCriteria: All: make a slider move in a slot
Most: make a lever turn on a pivot
Some: say how to improve my card
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: push and pull make things move
lessons.smsc: Social: making a gift to share with family

keywords.def: parts that work together to make something move
a strip that moves along a slot
a bar that turns around a point
the point a lever turns on
say what is good and what to improve

hook.text: Think of a toy that moves when you push or pull it. How does it work?

starter.q: A thick line is made by pressing:

starter.a: Straight, curved, thick, thin, zigzag or dotted

teach.heading: Sliders
bullets: Cut a slot in the card
Pull the strip to move the picture
teach.note: Show a bus sliding along a street. Safety: an adult cuts the slot.

teach.heading: Levers
bullets: A split pin is the pivot
Push the end and it turns
teach.note: Tower Bridge's road lifts up to let tall ships pass: we can copy that with a lever.

teach.heading: Make a bus slide
bullets: Put the strip in the slot
teach.note: Model the whole slider live on camera.

steps: Adult cuts a slot along the road
Glue the bus to a strip
Push the strip through the slot
model.answer: A bus that slides along the street

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: The split pin is the pivot; a slider moves in a slot.

practice.q: Which moves along a slot: a slider or a lever?
practice.model:
A slot is a long gap.
A strip moves along it.
That is a slider.

practice.q: What can we use as a pivot?
Which part of Tower Bridge lifts up?

independent.q: Core: Make a London card with a slider (a bus moving along a street) or a lever (Tower Bridge lifting).
independent.a: A card with one working mechanism
independent.model: Teacher shows the slider made on camera in the model step.

independent.q: Extend: Add a second moving part.
independent.a: A second slider or lever that works

independent.q: Stretch: Say one thing that went well and one thing to improve.
independent.a: For example: the bus slides well; the slot was too tight

exit.q: A split pin can be a:
exit.a: Pivot

exit.q: Big question: how can a picture move without batteries?
exit.a: With a mechanism such as a slider or a lever that we push or pull

lessons.homework: Give your moving card to a family member and show them how it works.
lessons.send: SEND: pre-cut strips and a slot cut by the adult. EAL: slider, lever, pivot with real examples. Stretch: make a lever with two pivots.

Moving card templates: bus and Tower Bridge (portal printable; no people)

lessons.unit: Summer 2: Sky painting and food (Splendid Skies and Chop, Slice & Mash)
lessons.title: Sky painting: tints and collage
lessons.bigQuestion: How many different blues can you see in the sky today?
objectives: To understand how to mix colours and lighter tints to paint a sky
successCriteria: All: mix a secondary colour from two primary colours
Most: make a tint by adding white
Some: add collage to give the sky texture
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the sky and weather we have been recording
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: noticing the beauty of the sky

keywords.def: red, yellow or blue: colours we cannot mix
a colour made by mixing two primary colours
a colour made lighter by adding white
a picture made by sticking on paper pieces
how something looks or feels: rough, smooth, fluffy

hook.text: Is the sky always blue? What other colours have you seen in it?

islamicLink.text: Allah asks us to look at the sky above us and how He built it and made it beautiful (Qaf 50:6). When we paint the sky, we look closely at what Allah has made.

teach.heading: Mixing colours
teach.note: Show each mix with paint on a plate. These are secondary colours.

teach.heading: Making tints
bullets: Add a tiny bit of colour
teach.note: Model: white first, then a dot of blue. It is easier to add colour to white than white to colour.

model.problem: Make three blues for a sky
steps: Add a dot of blue and mix
Add more blue for the next one
Paint dark at the top, light near the ground
model.answer: Three blues from dark to light

teach.heading: Add collage
bullets: Stick on clouds or a sunset
teach.note: Tearing gives soft edges like clouds. Glue lightly.

teach.heading: Check
teach.note: Share the results.

check.q: To make a lighter tint of blue, add:

get bigger

hook.text: If you had a garden, which fruit or vegetable would you grow, and why?

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us to look at our food: how He sends down rain and makes grain, grapes, olives, dates and fruit grow from the earth for us (Abasa 80:24-32). Every fruit and vegetable is a gift to be thankful for.

objectives: To understand how to prepare food safely and hygienically to make a simple dish
successCriteria: All: wash hands and keep the work area clean
Most: chop, slice or mash with an adult's help
Some: say what I would change next time
lessons.smsc: Social: preparing food to share with family

keywords.def: keeping clean so germs do not spread
cut into small pieces
cut into thin flat pieces
squash food until it is soft
say what went well and what to change

hook.text: If you made a fruit salad for your family, which three fruits would you choose?

islamicLink.text: Allah says: eat and drink, but do not waste (Al-A'raf 7:31). We make only what we can eat and share it with our family.

starter.q: Say one word to describe a banana.
starter.a: For example: soft, sweet or yellow

teach.heading: Clean first
teach.note: Germs can make us ill. Hygiene keeps food safe.

teach.heading: Safe cutting
bullets: An adult is always with you
Bridge hold: fingers on each side
teach.note: Model both holds with a banana and a table knife. Only cut with an adult's say-so.

steps: Cut down slowly between your fingers
Put the slices in the bowl

bullets: Mash a banana or avocado for a dip
teach.note: Mashing needs no knife, so it is a good first job.

teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Clean hands stop germs getting on food.

practice.q: What do we do first?
